title: What Buyers Really Want From a Business Sale
description: When you’re selling a business, it’s natural to focus on the number you want to receive. But experienced sellers know that a successful transaction involves much more than agreeing on a price. The amount of cash changing hands, the financing structure, the buyer’s ability to operate the business, and the expectations of both parties can all influence whether a deal actually comes together. The key is finding a structure that makes sense for both sides. A buyer may be willing to pay a strong price for a good business, but the amount of cash required upfront can have a significant impact on whether the transaction is workable. Seller financing can sometimes bridge that gap. Rather than requiring the buyer to provide the entire purchase price in cash at closing, a seller may finance a portion of the purchase. This can make the business accessible to a larger pool of qualified buyers while giving the seller the opportunity to receive payments over time. For buyers, the question is often simple: Can this business support the purchase price and provide enough income to make the investment worthwhile? For sellers, there’s a similar question: Can I structure the transaction in a way that gives the buyer a realistic chance to succeed while still achieving my financial goals? The best deal structure considers both. Qualified Buyers Matter Not every person who expresses interest in buying a business is ready or able to complete a transaction. A serious buyer should have a realistic understanding of the financial commitment involved, the responsibilities of ownership, and what it will take to operate the company successfully. This is one reason buyer qualification is such an important part of the selling process. A seller doesn’t simply need someone who likes the business. They need a buyer who has the financial resources, motivation, and ability to move forward. A qualified buyer also gives the seller greater confidence when considering terms such as seller financing. title: Stop being the last step ineveryprocess.
description: COMMON QUESTIONS Your questions, answered directly. If something is unclear after reading through these, the next step is a conversation. We want to understand where your practice is before recommending anything. START A CONVERSATION Do I have to take everything, or can I start with one piece? You start with either the website or the CRM. Deal management is its own software, tied to the CRM, so it arrives with the CRM rather than being a separate starting point. Whichever you begin with is built to connect to the rest, so adding the next piece later is an extension rather than a rebuild. Who designs and builds the website? The Deal Studio design team. It starts with a Brand Sprint to settle your positioning and messaging, then we handle the design, the build, the hosting, and the ongoing updates, and we wire it into your CRM as part of the build rather than afterward. What is a Brand Sprint? A focused working session before design starts. We work through who you serve, what you want to be known for, and how you talk about it, and the site gets built from what comes out of it. Its job is a website that says something specific about you from the day it launches rather than something generic. It is deliberately narrow: the Sprint settles the site, and it does not produce a brand guide. How is that different from a full brand engagement? Depth, and what comes out the other side. The Sprint settles positioning and messaging so the website can launch as something specific to you. A full brand engagement goes further: research into your market and the people you are trying to reach, positioning developed from the ground up, and a brand system built around connected outcomes, where one guide goes on to produce campaigns, content, resources, and new opportunities rather than a single website. description: COMMON QUESTIONS Your questions, answered directly. If something is unclear after reading through these, the next step is a conversation. We want to understand where your practice is before recommending anything. START A CONVERSATION Do I have to take everything, or can I start with one piece? You start with either the website or the CRM. Deal management is its own software, tied to the CRM, so it arrives with the CRM rather than being a separate starting point. Whichever you begin with is built to connect to the rest, so adding the next piece later is an extension rather than a rebuild. Who designs and builds the website? The Deal Studio design team. It starts with a Brand Sprint to settle your positioning and messaging, then we handle the design, the build, the hosting, and the ongoing updates, and we wire it into your CRM as part of the build rather than afterward. What is a Brand Sprint? A focused working session before design starts. We work through who you serve, what you want to be known for, and how you talk about it, and the site gets built from what comes out of it. Its job is a website that says something specific about you from the day it launches rather than something generic. It is deliberately narrow: the Sprint settles the site, and it does not produce a brand guide. How is that different from a full brand engagement? Depth, and what comes out the other side. The Sprint settles positioning and messaging so the website can launch as something specific to you. A full brand engagement goes further: research into your market and the people you are trying to reach, positioning developed from the ground up, and a brand system built around connected outcomes, where one guide goes on to produce campaigns, content, resources, and new opportunities rather than a single website. As a Partner in Patriot Mergers and Acquisitions, Bernie excels at listening to his clients and helping them navigate the complex process of Selling or Buying a business. Bernie applies his experiences and education from his roles at Fortune 100 companies, technology start-ups, and business ownership to help smooth the transition process. Bernie is an Accredited Business Intermediary who has successfully guided the transaction of multiple businesses to achieve the goals of both the seller and buyer. During his time at Purdue University, receiving degrees in technology and economics, he was also enlisted in the Army National Guard for 8 years. The ethics and discipline instilled in him during this time remains a foundation of Bernie’s daily life. In 2015, his long-time colleague and friend, Daren Henson, offered him a partnership in his business brokerage start-up. From the initiation of this partnership, Patriot Mergers and Acquisitions was born. Bernie is married to his wife Gena, a Texas native, and grateful to reside in Brenham, TX. Their kids consist of dogs, Longhorn cattle, donkeys, and horses. Bernie is also a professional horse trainer for over 20 years and now donates his time to various rescue associations to assist them with the recovery of neglected horses so they may become safe and adoptable. First and foremost, Bernie gives thanks to God for allowing him to use his skills to be a part of helping many busines

title: HVAC Company for Sale
description: Search Categories Categories Select Category As seen in St. Louis Small Business Monthly Building Value business for sale Buying A Business Maximizing your Sale Planning your Life Beyond Business Timely Topics Uncategorized HVAC Company for Sale S-2546 HVAC company St. Louis, Missouri Asking Price: $815,000 including inventory. Gross Revenue: $2 million Years in Business: 40+ Type of Sale: Asset Sale # of employees: 9 FT, 1 PT Business Description: This HVAC company has developed a reputation for consistent, quality residential HVAC service for nearly 40 years. They are recognized as the go-to resource for rehabbing existing systems or installing new systems in older St. Louis-area homes, including those with radiator heat. The company’s specialty is complex duct work design and installation, including homes with multiple systems. The business has benefitted from skilled union labor, reducing turnover and the need for inhouse training. Detailed Information: Market : Clientele is concentrated in affluent areas of St Louis City and County. The company has been relying on referrals for new clients, rather than traditional marketing. Growth/Expansion : A full-time salesperson would increase sales and remove that task from employees who are performing sales in addition to other duties. Add another installation crew to meet increased demand. Ideal Buyer Requirements : An owner background in the HVAC industry would provide a natural path to owning this business, however, the strong, knowledgeable leadership team that intends to remain with the company could also facilitate an absentee owner. The business is also an attractive expansion acquisition for a current HVAC or related company. Terms: Asset sale Real estate: Available for purchase Support/Training: Ownership is committed to providing up to 90 days as needed for systems training and transitioning of relationships. Reason Selling: Retirement Listed By: David Driscoll – Metro Business Advisors, LLC [email protected] L

title: Boutique Quilt Store
broker_name: bruce raw - will ogrady - mike russo
description: Boutique Quilt Store ASKING PRICE: $175,000 Plus cost of retail inventory CASH FLOW: $76,000 Hilton Head Island, South Carolina ​This is a charming, boutique quilt store located on beautiful Hilton Head Island, proudly serving the Lowcountry quilting community for many years. With a strong reputation for quality fabrics, expert advice, and exceptional customer service, this well-established business is a go-to destination for both local quilting enthusiasts and visiting crafters. Known for its warm, welcoming atmosphere and wide selection of premium fabrics, tools, and quilting supplies, Island Quilters has become a trusted resource and creative hub. Its steady location and loyal customer base provide a unique opportunity for a new owner to continue the tradition and passion for quilting that has been cultivated here for generations.

title: Wholesaler To The Gift Shop Market - SOLD
broker_name: bruce raw - will ogrady - mike russo
description: Wholesaler To The Gift Shop Market - SOLD ASKING PRICE: $345,000 including inventory CASH FLOW: $155,000 Hilton Head, South Carolina This business offers a unique, made-to-order wholesale model with a proven track record of serving the gift shop market. Unlike traditional operators, the company maintains an inventory of base products, allowing for high customization and low overhead. The production workflow is fully integrated, utilizing spray painting, decoupage, easy clay work, and assembly to transform raw materials into premium, retail-ready goods. With a streamlined transition from order to final assembly, this brand represents a turnkey opportunity for a buyer looking to acquire a creative business with established production processes and a loyal client base.  Owner need not have specialized skill and artistic ability.

broker_name: bruce raw - will ogrady - mike russo
description: Hilton Head Island , South Carolina and Savannah, Georgia ​This is a rare opportunity to acquire an established DogWatch of Savannah and Hilton Head Island franchise (in 9 rapidly growing dog loving counties) with a proven 7-year operating history and a median gross revenue of $175,000 while maintaining very low overhead. The business benefits from an exclusive, protected territory in two highly desirable and growing coastal markets, ensuring limited competition and consistent demand for premium pet containment solutions. With a loyal customer base, strong brand recognition, and an efficient operating model, this turnkey franchise offers immediate cash flow and significant potential for expansion through increased marketing, additional service offerings, and untapped residential and commercial accounts, making it an ideal investment for an owner-operator or strategic buyer seeking both stability and growth. title: We Know TheRestaurant Business
description: Frequently Asked Questions ​ What does a restaurant broker do? A restaurant broker manages the full process of buying, selling, or leasing a restaurant business or food & beverage space. This includes business valuation , confidential marketing, buyer qualification, lease review, and negotiation — from listing to closing. ​ Why should I use a restaurant broker instead of a general real estate agent? A restaurant broker specializes exclusively in food & beverage transactions, bringing operational knowledge, industry contacts, and valuation expertise that a general real estate agent simply doesn't have. Jimmy Carey has 37 years of restaurant industry experience as a former chef and multi-unit operator — he has sat on both sides of the table. ​ How much is my Atlanta restaurant worth? Restaurant value in Atlanta is determined primarily by Seller's Discretionary Earnings (SDE) — not revenue, not square footage. Most profitable Atlanta restaurants sell for 2x to 3x SDE. A proper valuation requires a full financial recast, not just a tax return review. ​ Recent examples: A Sandy Springs sushi restaurant sold at 2.4x SDE. An Atlanta pizzeria closed at 2.48x SDE in under four months. Atlanta restaurant valuations consistently range from 2x to 3x SDE for profitable concepts with clean financials and an assignable lease. ​ Do you only serve Atlanta, or do you work throughout Georgia? Jimmy Carey Commercial Real Estate serves Atlanta, Savannah, and all of Georgia. Whether you are selling a restaurant in Buckhead, looking for space in Savannah's Historic District , or exploring opportunities anywhere in the state, we handle the full transaction. ​ How do I get started selling my restaurant confidentially? The process begins with a confidential consultation — no obligation, no public listing, no staff awareness. title: M&A AdvisoryforBusiness ServicesFounders
description: Frequently Asked Common Questions from Business Services Founders What size business services firms does Valorem Advisors work with? We focus on founder-owned staffing, consulting, accounting, MSP, agency, training, and subscription-based service businesses with $5M–$50M in annual revenue and $1M–$5M+ in EBITDA. These firms are large enough to attract strategic consolidators, professional-services PE, and family-office capital, but still benefit from the personalized attention of a boutique M&A advisory firm. What business services sub-sectors do you advise? Staffing and recruiting, B2B consulting and boutique advisory, accounting and bookkeeping, IT managed services, digital marketing and creative agencies, B2B training and education, and subscription-based B2B services. Each sub-sector has its own buyer pool, its own value drivers, and its own multiple range, and we calibrate the process accordingly. My firm is a personal-services business where I'm the rainmaker. Is it sellable? Often yes, but the work has to start two to three years ahead of going to market. The most common reason a services firm fails to sell is founder dependency: clients stay because of the founder's relationship, sales come from the founder's calendar, and key processes live in the founder's head. Pre-sale advisory work focuses on reducing each of those dependencies: distributing client relationships, productizing acquisition, and documenting process, so the firm becomes tradeable. We've seen the difference between a $5M services firm that sells at 4x and one that sells at 7x come down to exactly this. Will my customers, team, or competitors find out we're exploring a sale? No. Confidentiality is built into the process from day one. No public listing on any marketplace. Buyer outreach is direct and targeted, with no firm name, client list, or financials shared before an NDA is signed. title: Sell Your Companyfor What It'sActually Worth
description: Common Questions Questions Owners Ask Us Straight answers to what sellers want to know before they ever pick up the phone. What size companies does Valorem Advisors work with? We focus on founder-owned and family-owned companies generating roughly $5M to $50M in annual revenue, or $1M+ in EBITDA. Smaller Main Street businesses are served through Valorem Business Brokers. How is M&A advisory different from listing my business with a broker? A broker lists and waits. We run a confidential, competitive process: institutional valuation, targeted outreach to qualified strategic and financial buyers, and managed bidding designed to create tension and drive enterprise value. The goal is a premium outcome, not a quick sale. Will my employees, customers, or competitors find out my company is for sale? No. Every buyer interaction is gated behind a structured NDA process. We never contact your employees, customers, or competitors without your explicit permission, and your identity stays protected until you choose to reveal it. What is my business worth? Lower middle market companies are typically valued on a multiple of EBITDA or SDE, adjusted for growth, customer concentration, management depth, and recurring revenue. We provide a confidential Broker Opinion of Value so you know your number before you decide anything. How long does it take to sell a lower middle market company? A typical sell-side process runs six to twelve months from engagement to close, depending on financial readiness, the buyer universe, and diligence. Owners who prepare 12–36 months ahead usually sell faster and for more. When should I start the conversation if I want to sell in a few years? Sooner than you think. The owners who capture the highest values start 12 to 36 months out, giving us time to close value gaps, reduce key-person risk, and clean up financials before going to market. title: Confidential Business BrokerageforOwner-Operators
description: Frequently Asked Common Questions from Main Street Owners What size businesses does Valorem Business Brokers represent? Our brokerage practice focuses on owner-operated South Florida service businesses with sale prices from $250,000 to $5 million, typically generating $100,000 to $1 million in Seller's Discretionary Earnings (SDE). For businesses with $5M+ in revenue and $1M+ in EBITDA, we run a separate lower middle market M&A advisory process under our Valorem Advisors practice . How long does it take to sell a Main Street business? From engagement to closing, a well-prepared business with clean books typically takes 6 to 12 months. The valuation and CIM build takes 2 to 4 weeks, marketing and buyer screening runs 60 to 120 days, due diligence and SBA underwriting adds another 60 to 90 days, and closing closes out the timeline. Businesses with messy financials, customer concentration, or heavy owner dependency take longer or sometimes don't sell at all without preparation work upfront. What is my business worth? Main Street businesses are most commonly valued as a multiple of Seller's Discretionary Earnings (SDE) — typically 2.0x to 3.5x, depending on vertical, recurring revenue, customer concentration, owner separability, and growth runway. We start every engagement with a no-cost Broker's Opinion of Value (BOV) that establishes a defensible range using your last three years of financials, comparable closed transactions in your vertical, and current SBA-financed buyer activity. Will my customers, team, or competitors find out we're selling? No. Every Valorem engagement is fully confidential. There is no public listing under your business name on any marketplace. Buyer outreach uses a blind teaser only — no company name, no client list, no financials — until a buyer signs an NDA and is qualified financially. title: Kelleher & Sadowsky Associates Inc.
description:
About us Kelleher & Sadowsky has been serving the Worcester and Central Massachusetts market since 1981 and began expanding east towards Boston during 2020. During this time we have earned a reputation as the area’s premier commercial real estate company by forging strong relationships with landlords, tenants, and a wide network of business leaders. We have consistently achieved outstanding results for our clients while conducting our business with the highest level of integrity.

Kelleher & Sadowsky’s brokers specialize in a wide variety of core property types: office, industrial, medical, retail, multi-family, land, along with investment opportunities. We ensure the most adept market specialists at our firm are working with you on each of your specific commercial real estate transactions. Our core services include brokerage services, landlord and tenant representation, investment sales, and consulting.

We interact daily with qualified commercial real estate firms on both a local and national level. Our affiliations with the following local, regional and national organizations assist us in providing high quality service to our clients and customers. Whether you are buying your first home, buying a business opportunity or selling your multi-tenant commercial property. We are committed to assist you each and every step of the way to achieve the best results. In today’s real estate market, selling and buying a property requires advanced knowledge of online as well as traditional marketing platforms. Just having a real estate license and listing a property on the MLS is not enough – you want an agent who has their ear to the ground when it comes to market trends, a deep understanding of the communities they serve, and the ability to think outside the box. title: What Buyers Really Want From a Business Sale - Foresight Business Brokers
description: When you’re selling a business, it’s natural to focus on the number you want to receive. But experienced sellers know that a successful transaction involves much more than agreeing on a price. The amount of cash changing hands, the financing structure, the buyer’s ability to operate the business, and the expectations of both parties can all influence whether a deal actually comes together. The key is finding a structure that makes sense for both sides. A buyer may be willing to pay a strong price for a good business, but the amount of cash required upfront can have a significant impact on whether the transaction is workable. Seller financing can sometimes bridge that gap. Rather than requiring the buyer to provide the entire purchase price in cash at closing, a seller may finance a portion of the purchase. This can make the business accessible to a larger pool of qualified buyers while giving the seller the opportunity to receive payments over time. For buyers, the question is often simple: Can this business support the purchase price and provide enough income to make the investment worthwhile? For sellers, there’s a similar question: Can I structure the transaction in a way that gives the buyer a realistic chance to succeed while still achieving my financial goals? The best deal structure considers both. Qualified Buyers Matter Not every person who expresses interest in buying a business is ready or able to complete a transaction. A serious buyer should have a realistic understanding of the financial commitment involved, the responsibilities of ownership, and what it will take to operate the company successfully. This is one reason buyer qualification is such an important part of the selling process. A seller doesn’t simply need someone who likes the business. They need a buyer who has the financial resources, motivation, and ability to move forward. A qualified buyer also gives the seller greater confidence when considering terms such as seller financing. title: Does Your Asking Price Help or Hurt Your Business Sale? - Foresight Business Brokers
description: Seller Articles Does Your Asking Price Help or Hurt Your Business Sale? by Deal Studio on September 18, 2026 One of the most important decisions a business owner makes when preparing to sell is determining the right asking price. It is natural to want the highest possible value for a company built through years of hard work, sacrifice, and dedication. However, the market ultimately determines what a business is worth. Setting an asking price based on the company’s financial performance, strengths, and current market conditions is one of the best ways to attract qualified buyers. Some sellers take the approach of starting with a higher asking price and lowering it later if necessary. While this may seem like a reasonable strategy, it can create challenges. Buyers often use the asking price as their first indication of whether a business is a realistic opportunity. If the price does not align with the company’s earnings, assets, and market value, many qualified buyers may never take the time to explore further. An overpriced business can also spend more time on the market, causing buyers to question why it has not sold. A realistic asking price, on the other hand, can create more interest, encourage serious conversations, and lead to stronger negotiations. Determining the right price requires looking beyond what an owner hopes to receive. Buyers evaluate factors such as profitability, revenue trends, customer relationships, growth opportunities, operational systems, and risk. Two businesses in the same industry can have very different values depending on how they perform and how well they are positioned for future success. A business broker can provide valuable perspective throughout this process. Because brokers regularly work with buyers and sellers, they understand market conditions, buyer expectations, and the factors that influence value. title: What Makes a Business Attractive to Buyers? - Foresight Business Brokers
description: Seller Articles What Makes a Business Attractive to Buyers? by Deal Studio on September 11, 2026 Many business owners wonder whether their industry will determine how easy it is to sell their business. While certain industries may experience periods of higher demand than others, buyers rarely make decisions based on industry alone. More often, they focus on the quality of the business itself. A well-managed company with strong financial performance will generally attract more interest than a struggling business in a “hot” industry. Understanding what buyers value can help owners make improvements long before they decide to sell. Buyers Look Beyond the Industry Every buyer has unique goals. Some are looking to expand an existing business, while others want to become business owners for the first time. Investment groups may be searching for companies with strong cash flow, while strategic buyers may value opportunities to grow through acquisition. Despite these different motivations, most buyers evaluate businesses using many of the same criteria. They want confidence that the business can continue to succeed after the ownership transition. Consistent profitability is often at the top of the list. Buyers also appreciate reliable cash flow, accurate financial records, and a business that has demonstrated stable performance over time. These factors help reduce uncertainty and make it easier for buyers and lenders to evaluate the opportunity. Characteristics That Increase Buyer Interest Businesses that generate recurring or repeat revenue often stand out because they provide greater predictability. Long-term customer relationships, recurring service agreements, or repeat purchasing patterns can all make future income more dependable. Buyers also look favorably on businesses that are not overly dependent on the owner. description: COMMON QUESTIONS Your questions, answered directly. If something is unclear after reading through these, the next step is a conversation. We want to understand where your practice is before recommending anything. START A CONVERSATION Do I have to take everything, or can I start with one piece? You start with either the website or the CRM. Deal management is its own software, tied to the CRM, so it arrives with the CRM rather than being a separate starting point. Whichever you begin with is built to connect to the rest, so adding the next piece later is an extension rather than a rebuild. Who designs and builds the website? The Deal Studio design team. It starts with a Brand Sprint to settle your positioning and messaging, then we handle the design, the build, the hosting, and the ongoing updates, and we wire it into your CRM as part of the build rather than afterward. What is a Brand Sprint? A focused working session before design starts. We work through who you serve, what you want to be known for, and how you talk about it, and the site gets built from what comes out of it. Its job is a website that says something specific about you from the day it launches rather than something generic. It is deliberately narrow: the Sprint settles the site, and it does not produce a brand guide. How is that different from a full brand engagement? Depth, and what comes out the other side. The Sprint settles positioning and messaging so the website can launch as something specific to you. A full brand engagement goes further: research into your market and the people you are trying to reach, positioning developed from the ground up, and a brand system built around connected outcomes, where one guide goes on to produce campaigns, content, resources, and new opportunities rather than a single website. title: BENEFITS & INCOME POTENTIAL
description: BENEFITS & INCOME POTENTIAL Owning a pool route business can be very rewarding. If you are looking for a better career or to sell your pool accounts, we can make it happen. We have full-time and part-time pool routes for sale in your area. We are one of the top Pool Route Brokers in the country. With over 30 years combined industry experience, we can help find a pool route that is right for you. Benefits Of The Pool Route Business Service businesses are Recession Proof Predictable monthly cash flow from service customers You don’t work nights or weekends The pool service business is easy to learn Very low startup costs Support for new pool service professionals Income Potential There are two main areas of income in owning a Pool Route Business. Monthly Pool Service Billing Income Repairs / Maintenance Income A pool service professional will make about $50 – $60 per hour cleaning and servicing pools. That amount will increase to $150 – $200 per hour doing minor repairs/maintenance on the pool equipment. The expenses to run a pool service business should be about 20% of the monthly service billing amount. The primary expenses in a pool service business are pool chemicals, gas, insurance and office supplies. The average pool route business owner, running the route correctly should have a yearly net income (income after expenses) of $80,000 to $100,000+ per year. This net income amount will vary slightly depending on the average service rates for the area. The key to running a pool service route correctly is keeping the expenses to a minimum and making sure you are charging the proper rates for pool service in your area. You can help keep expenses lower by running your business out of your house, using a small truck to save on gas and shopping the different suppliers for the best prices on chemicals and equipment. Income Example: A pool service professional with a monthly service billing amount of $6,000 receives $72,000 per year servicing/cleaning pools. As stated abov

description:
BUYER INQUIRY & FAQ Buyer Frequently Asked Questions Q: Why should I buy a pool route through SpringBoard PRB? A: Well, there are many reasons to buy a route through us. We have many years of extensive hands-on experience in the pool service and financial services industries. title: What Buyers Really Want From a Business Sale - Colorado Business Brokers
description: When you’re selling a business, it’s natural to focus on the number you want to receive. But experienced sellers know that a successful transaction involves much more than agreeing on a price. The amount of cash changing hands, the financing structure, the buyer’s ability to operate the business, and the expectations of both parties can all influence whether a deal actually comes together. The key is finding a structure that makes sense for both sides. A buyer may be willing to pay a strong price for a good business, but the amount of cash required upfront can have a significant impact on whether the transaction is workable. Seller financing can sometimes bridge that gap. Rather than requiring the buyer to provide the entire purchase price in cash at closing, a seller may finance a portion of the purchase. This can make the business accessible to a larger pool of qualified buyers while giving the seller the opportunity to receive payments over time. For buyers, the question is often simple: Can this business support the purchase price and provide enough income to make the investment worthwhile? For sellers, there’s a similar question: Can I structure the transaction in a way that gives the buyer a realistic chance to succeed while still achieving my financial goals? The best deal structure considers both. Qualified Buyers Matter Not every person who expresses interest in buying a business is ready or able to complete a transaction. A serious buyer should have a realistic understanding of the financial commitment involved, the responsibilities of ownership, and what it will take to operate the company successfully. This is one reason buyer qualification is such an important part of the selling process. A seller doesn’t simply need someone who likes the business. title: What Buyers Really Want From a Business Sale - Colorado Business Brokers
description: When you’re selling a business, it’s natural to focus on the number you want to receive. But experienced sellers know that a successful transaction involves much more than agreeing on a price. The amount of cash changing hands, the financing structure, the buyer’s ability to operate the business, and the expectations of both parties can all influence whether a deal actually comes together. The key is finding a structure that makes sense for both sides. A buyer may be willing to pay a strong price for a good business, but the amount of cash required upfront can have a significant impact on whether the transaction is workable. Seller financing can sometimes bridge that gap. Rather than requiring the buyer to provide the entire purchase price in cash at closing, a seller may finance a portion of the purchase. This can make the business accessible to a larger pool of qualified buyers while giving the seller the opportunity to receive payments over time. For buyers, the question is often simple: Can this business support the purchase price and provide enough income to make the investment worthwhile? For sellers, there’s a similar question: Can I structure the transaction in a way that gives the buyer a realistic chance to succeed while still achieving my financial goals? The best deal structure considers both. Qualified Buyers Matter Not every person who expresses interest in buying a business is ready or able to complete a transaction. A serious buyer should have a realistic understanding of the financial commitment involved, the responsibilities of ownership, and what it will take to operate the company successfully. This is one reason buyer qualification is such an important part of the selling process. A seller doesn’t simply need someone who likes the business. They need a buyer who has the financial resources, motivation, and ability to move forward. A qualified buyer also gives the seller greater confidence when considering terms such as seller financing. title: Does Your Asking Price Help or Hurt Your Business Sale? - Colorado Business Brokers
description: Seller Articles Does Your Asking Price Help or Hurt Your Business Sale? by Deal Studio on September 18, 2026 One of the most important decisions a business owner makes when preparing to sell is determining the right asking price. It is natural to want the highest possible value for a company built through years of hard work, sacrifice, and dedication. However, the market ultimately determines what a business is worth. Setting an asking price based on the company’s financial performance, strengths, and current market conditions is one of the best ways to attract qualified buyers. Some sellers take the approach of starting with a higher asking price and lowering it later if necessary. While this may seem like a reasonable strategy, it can create challenges. Buyers often use the asking price as their first indication of whether a business is a realistic opportunity. If the price does not align with the company’s earnings, assets, and market value, many qualified buyers may never take the time to explore further. An overpriced business can also spend more time on the market, causing buyers to question why it has not sold. A realistic asking price, on the other hand, can create more interest, encourage serious conversations, and lead to stronger negotiations. Determining the right price requires looking beyond what an owner hopes to receive. Buyers evaluate factors such as profitability, revenue trends, customer relationships, growth opportunities, operational systems, and risk. Two businesses in the same industry can have very different values depending on how they perform and how well they are positioned for future success. A business broker can provide valuable perspective throughout this process. Because brokers regularly work with buyers and sellers, they understand market conditions, buyer expectations, and the factors that influence value. title: What Makes a Business Attractive to Buyers? - Colorado Business Brokers
description: Seller Articles What Makes a Business Attractive to Buyers? by Deal Studio on September 11, 2026 Many business owners wonder whether their industry will determine how easy it is to sell their business. While certain industries may experience periods of higher demand than others, buyers rarely make decisions based on industry alone. More often, they focus on the quality of the business itself. A well-managed company with strong financial performance will generally attract more interest than a struggling business in a “hot” industry. Understanding what buyers value can help owners make improvements long before they decide to sell. Buyers Look Beyond the Industry Every buyer has unique goals. Some are looking to expand an existing business, while others want to become business owners for the first time. Investment groups may be searching for companies with strong cash flow, while strategic buyers may value opportunities to grow through acquisition. Despite these different motivations, most buyers evaluate businesses using many of the same criteria. They want confidence that the business can continue to succeed after the ownership transition. Consistent profitability is often at the top of the list. Buyers also appreciate reliable cash flow, accurate financial records, and a business that has demonstrated stable performance over time. These factors help reduce uncertainty and make it easier for buyers and lenders to evaluate the opportunity. Characteristics That Increase Buyer Interest Businesses that generate recurring or repeat revenue often stand out because they provide greater predictability. Long-term customer relationships, recurring service agreements, or repeat purchasing patterns can all make future income more dependable. Buyers also look favorably on businesses that are not overly dependent on the owner. title: Quality management systems - ISO 9001
description: Quality management systems - ISO 9001 Introduction ISO 9001 is the ultimate global benchmark for quality management and a critical tool for boosting your company’s success, profitability and market potential. ISO 9001:2015 specifies requirements for a quality management system a) needs to demonstrate its ability to consistently provide products and services that meet customer and applicable statutory and regulatory requirements, and b) aim to enhance customer satisfaction through the effective application of the system, including processes for improvement of the system and the assurance of conformity to customer and applicable statutory and regulatory requirements. All the requirements of ISO 9001:2015 are generic and are intended to be applicable to any organization, regardless of its type or size, or the products and services it provides. How will it help my business? The ultimate global benchmark for quality management will: 1. Open your business to the local and international market. 2. The ability to be involved with Tenders more professionality. 3. Cost Saving and containment. 4. Better internal processes. 5. Understanding customer needs and future requirements. 6. Staff motivation is improved through greater clarity. 7. Focusing on business objectives and developing the business. 8. Save time and resource. 9. Improving your customer service. 10. Having continues customer referrals. What is ISO 9001? ISO 9001 is an international standard that focuses on customer satisfaction, the ability to provide products and/or services that meet the internal and external requirements of the organization so that its performance can be controlled and improved, drive to excellence and efficiency, and optimize customer support. . Why to get the ISO 9001 certificate? The ISO 9001 is the most recognized worldwide Quality Standard. Can you assist our company to get the ISO certificate? title: Stop being the last step ineveryprocess.
description: COMMON QUESTIONS Your questions, answered directly. If something is unclear after reading through these, the next step is a conversation. We want to understand where your practice is before recommending anything. START A CONVERSATION Do I have to take everything, or can I start with one piece? You start with either the website or the CRM. Deal management is its own software, tied to the CRM, so it arrives with the CRM rather than being a separate starting point. Whichever you begin with is built to connect to the rest, so adding the next piece later is an extension rather than a rebuild. Who designs and builds the website? The Deal Studio design team. It starts with a Brand Sprint to settle your positioning and messaging, then we handle the design, the build, the hosting, and the ongoing updates, and we wire it into your CRM as part of the build rather than afterward. What is a Brand Sprint? A focused working session before design starts. We work through who you serve, what you want to be known for, and how you talk about it, and the site gets built from what comes out of it. Its job is a website that says something specific about you from the day it launches rather than something generic. It is deliberately narrow: the Sprint settles the site, and it does not produce a brand guide. How is that different from a full brand engagement? Depth, and what comes out the other side. The Sprint settles positioning and messaging so the website can launch as something specific to you. A full brand engagement goes further: research into your market and the people you are trying to reach, positioning developed from the ground up, and a brand system built around connected outcomes, where one guide goes on to produce campaigns, content, resources, and new opportunities rather than a single website. title: What Buyers Really Want From a Business Sale
description: Seller Articles What Buyers Really Want From a Business Sale September 25, 2026 When you’re selling a business, it’s natural to focus on the number you want to receive. But experienced sellers know that a successful transaction involves much more than agreeing on a price. The amount of cash changing hands, the financing structure, the buyer’s ability to operate the business, and the expectations of both parties can all influence whether a deal actually comes together. The key is finding a structure that makes sense for both sides. A buyer may be willing to pay a strong price for a good business, but the amount of cash required upfront can have a significant impact on whether the transaction is workable. Seller financing can sometimes bridge that gap. Rather than requiring the buyer to provide the entire purchase price in cash at closing, a seller may finance a portion of the purchase. This can make the business accessible to a larger pool of qualified buyers while giving the seller the opportunity to receive payments over time. For buyers, the question is often simple: Can this business support the purchase price and provide enough income to make the investment worthwhile? For sellers, there’s a similar question: Can I structure the transaction in a way that gives the buyer a realistic chance to succeed while still achieving my financial goals? The best deal structure considers both. Qualified Buyers Matter Not every person who expresses interest in buying a business is ready or able to complete a transaction. A serious buyer should have a realistic understanding of the financial commitment involved, the responsibilities of ownership, and what it will take to operate the company successfully. This is one reason buyer qualification is such an important part of the selling process. A seller doesn’t simply need someone who likes the business. They need a buyer who has the financial resources, motivation, and ability to move forward. A qualified buyer also gives the sel

September 18, 2026 One of the most important decisions a business owner makes when preparing to sell is determining the right asking price. It is natural to want the highest possible value for a company built through years of hard work, sacrifice, and dedication. However, the market ultimately determines what a business is worth. Setting an asking price based on the company’s financial performance, strengths, and current market conditions is one of the best ways to attract qualified buyers. Some sellers take the approach of starting with a higher asking price and lowering it later if necessary. While this may seem like a reasonable strategy, it can create challenges. Buyers often use the asking price as their first indication of whether a business is a realistic opportunity. September 11, 2026 Many business owners wonder whether their industry will determine how easy it is to sell their business. While certain industries may experience periods of higher demand than others, buyers rarely make decisions based on industry alone. More often, they focus on the quality of the business itself. A well-managed company with strong financial performance will generally attract more interest than a struggling business in a “hot” industry. Understanding what buyers value can help owners make improvements long before they decide to sell. Buyers Look Beyond the Industry Every buyer has unique goals. title: Car Wash, Storage Unit & Income Producing Retail - Commercial Package
description: Positioned just off a busy highway, this rare triple-income commercial opportunity combines convenience, character, and cash flow in one dynamic location. The property features a well-established car wash, a thriving antique mall with built-in vendor income, and a versatile storage/shop building—offering multiple revenue streams under one package. With strong visibility, steady traffic, and flexible space for expansion or repositioning, this property is ideal for investors or owner-operators seeking a diversified, income-producing asset with long-term upside. Asking price includes real estate of three buildings and associated businesses. Owner will not split business operations from real estate and would like to sell all together. Call 417.889.9400 today for a showing!

title: Automobile Restoration
description: A rare opportunity to acquire one of the Midwest’s most respected and nationally recognized classic automobile restoration companies. Established 28 years ago, this Missouri-based business has built an exceptional reputation for quality craftsmanship, attention to detail, and customer satisfaction. The company performs everything from routine maintenance and minor repairs to complete frame-off restoration for virtually any make, model, and year of vehicle. Its award-worthy work has been featured at some of the most prestigious automotive venues in the nation, including Barrett-Jackson, Mecum and SEMA.

title: Nationally Recognized Beauty and Health Franchise
description: Take advantage of this exceptional opportunity to acquire a Nationally Recognized Franchise celebrated by Entrepreneur Magazine. The location offers PRIME visibility, strong demographics and a built-in customer base. Consistent revenue performance and a loyal recurring clientele. This turnkey operation provides immediate cash flow and the backing of a proven national brand.

title: Service Center and Truck Repair Business
description: 2025 was a financial success and a great year for this business! This is a rare opportunity to acquire a well-established, highly respected commercial truck repair business located in Southern Missouri. In operation for 12 years, this business has built a solid reputation for quality service, reliability, and professionalism in a market with very little competition. The business operates out of a clean and efficiently organized facility featuring four oversized bays with 16-foot doors—capable of accommodating full-size tractor trailers. All equipment required to perform comprehensive truck repairs is included in the sale, along with a large, well-stocked inventory of essential parts and supplies. A team of five skilled technicians supports the operation, and the business is a preferred repair provider for multiple commercial fleet accounts. Mobile/remote service capabilities offer additional revenue and convenience for clients. This turnkey operation is ideal for an owner-operator or an industry buyer looking to expand. The current owner is pursuing other interests and is committed to a flexible and smooth transition for the new owner.

title: Beauty Salon and Tattoo Shop
description: This well-established beauty studio offers a comprehensive suite of high-demand services, including eyelash extensions, brow shaping, microblading, facials, tattoo removal, and permanent makeup. The studio is recognized for its clean, modern aesthetic and consistently high standards of service, resulting in an exceptional reputation and strong brand presence in the market. A key asset of this business is its large client database of over 7,000 active and past clients, providing immediate access to a large, loyal customer base and significant built-in opportunities for repeat business, reactivation campaigns, and service expansion. The studio benefits from steady recurring revenue, strong word-of-mouth referrals, and established operating systems. This is a rare opportunity for a beauty professional to acquire a profitable, turnkey studio with proven demand, recognizable branding, and substantial growth potential from an existing client base.

title: Auto Glass Business
description: This well-established auto glass repair and replacement business has built a trusted reputation across Southwest Missouri for quality, reliability, and personalized service. With a strong local brand and consistent repeat business, the company has operated success-fully for many years, serving retail customers, insurance claims, and a growing number of commercial and fleet accounts. The business offers mobile service capability, enabling flexible scheduling and efficient geographic coverage without the heavy overhead of multiple facilities. It is ideally positioned for continued growth through fleet and dealership partnerships, insurance referral programs, and expanded regional marketing.

title: Profitable Italian American Restaurant
description: PRICE REDUCTION. Owner wants to retire! This restaurant is growing. Revenue and profitability are increasing. The restaurant has been in its current location for over seven years and has been a trusted brand in the region for 13 years. With a loyal customer base, strong community ties, and a reputation for mouthwatering classics like hand-tossed pizzas, hearty pastas, and signature entrees, this turnkey operation is perfect for a new Owner or investor looking to step into a proven, profitable business. This opportunity is in SW Missouri. The owner wants the business to continue to prosper and will support the new owner through the transition process.

title: Coffee Business & Commercial Real Estate
description: Own an established drive-thru coffee business along with the commercial real estate. Operating since 2018, this turnkey opportunity includes the equipment, inventory, staff and property - giving a new owner the foundation to step in a continue serving the community. The experienced owner is committed to a smooth transition. Request an NDA to learn more about this business!

title: Retail Scooter Business
description: Family-owned retail scooter business in Southwest Missouri for sale. Serving the region for years, this business has built a strong reputation as a trusted transportation alternative - offering affordable and fuel-efficient scooters. The business is committed to customer satisfaction, setting itself apart with an in-house service center. Partnered with top suppliers, they have direct access to factory parts ensuring a quick turnaround and reliable maintenance for every customer. Take the keys to reliable and growing transportation in SW Missouri where great service and dependable products drive results.

title: Festus Jack's Restaurant & Historic Main Street Building
description: This restaurant is a destination for homemade comfort food, smoked barbeque, and genuine Ozark hospitality. With an established customer base, highly engaged Facebook following, fully equipped commercial kitchen, trained staff, and memorable dining atmosphere, a new owner can step into a true turnkey operation with significant room for growth. Current owners have only owned since end of 2024 and health concerns are forcing the sale.

title: Subway Sandwich Shop
description: This is a great opportunity to own an established Subway Sub Shop.  Located right on the cuff of Missouri State University. It has been in operation for 38 years!  Nothing like having a potential labor force of 23,000 students within a 2 mile radius!  All equipment is in excellent condition and is serviced regularly.  Current owners run the business in a passive manner and do no outside advertising.  A new owner/operator with some creative advertising & marketing would have HUGE growth potential by adding corporate catering, and networking with the surrounding businesses!  This business has so much growth potential based on location alone.  This Subway restaurant is great for a family or perfect for a husband/wife team.  Call to discuss this must-see business that will not disappoint.  Seller will entertain all reasonable offers.

title: Auto Body Shop
description: Auto Body Shop located in St. Louis, Missouri. This business has been around for over 45 years, has solid long-term customers and is in a fantastic high traffic location. Very solid back log of business and known for their quality craftmanship with timely service. This business is being offered at basically asset value which makes it an opportunity that can't be missed. The owners are retiring and will agree to a smooth and easy transition. Contact me directly for more information.

title: The Review Shoppe
description: For more than 35 years, The Review Shoppe has been Springfield's premier destination for upscale designer consignment. Established in 1990, the boutique has built a loyal following through carefully curated women's apparel, handbags, shoes, jewelry and accessories. Known for authenticity, exceptional customer service and extensive network of consigners, the business has become one of Southwest Missouri's most recognized upscale resale boutiques.

title: The Laser Studio
description: Established Aesthetic & Wellness Studio with Strong 2026 Performance This is an opportunity to acquire an established Springfield aesthetics and wellness studio operating since 2018. The business offers a diverse mix of non-invasive aesthetic and wellness services, including laser hair removal, body sculpting, skin rejuvenation, skin tightening, teeth whitening and other wellness treatments. The Springfield location generated $183,024 in revenue and $49,241 in Seller's Discretionary Earnings (SDE) in 2025. Performance has strengthened in 2026, with approximately $126,571 in revenue and $55,478 in SDE through July 2026. The $100,000 asking price includes approximately $76,000 in seller-estimated equipment and assets, providing a well-equipped, turnkey opportunity for an owner-operator, industry professional or entrepreneur looking to enter or expand within the aesthetics and wellness industry. The business currently has a trained employee in place. Assets from the seller's Joplin location are also available separately for an additional $20,000. The Joplin offering is asset-only and is not included in the financials.

title: Subway Sandwich Shop
description: This is a great opportunity to own an established Subway Sub Shop. All equipment is in excellent condition and is serviced regularly. Current owners run the business in a passive manner and do no outside advertising. This Subway restaurant is great for a family or perfect for a husband/wife team.

title: Restaurant & Bar with Bowling Alley
description: Summary Description Sited in one of New England’s premier outdoor recreation destinations, this is a newly built-out restaurant, bar, and family entertainment concept seeking a new ownership group to maximize its attractive foundation. For an established brand or portfolio operator, this acquisition represents a seamless entry into a lucrative market with all the heavy lifting of construction, permitting, and build-out already completed.

title: Recurring Revenue Home Services Provider
description: Summary Description This home services provider serves the Southern Maine market, including Greater Portland. The business has a year-over-year renewal rate of 80%+ across its customer base, with the vast majority on annual service contracts. The company is entering the second year of offering a significant product line extension, while also developing a substantial secondary target market for both its traditional and new service offerings. The business possesses a large base of customers within a tight radius around its location, and a new owner would have ample opportunity to grow the business’s presence outside of that area.

title: Dynamic Direct In-Home Care Services Provider
description: Summary Description This growing, highly profitable business, featuring a skilled and well-established workforce, offers a unique opportunity to gain access to a significant economic sector. Located in Southern Maine and providing in-home care services throughout the state, the business meets customer needs with excellence. Catering to a substantial niche market, the company delivers impressive net margins and has considerable room to grow - both in geographic reach and in the range of services provided.

description: Summary Description Entrenched as the premier local flooring company in one of New England’s most desirable markets, this well-established business offers a full complement of residential and commercial flooring solutions, including carpet, hardwood, tile, and vinyl. The business is turnkey, with a built-out showroom, curated inventory, and an experienced staff in a prime, heavily-trafficked location.

title: Southern Maine Food Services, Events and Catering
description: Summary Description With decades of experience, this Southern Maine-based, full-service food services, event planning and catering team excels at executing weddings, corporate gatherings, milestone celebrations, and social events across Southern Maine and Northern New England. Drawing on a skilled staff of chefs, bartenders, servers, and planners, they collaborate with top-tier vendors to seamlessly manage logistics for a wide range of venues and client needs.

title: What Buyers Really Want From a Business Sale - Northwest Business Brokers LLC
description: When you’re selling a business, it’s natural to focus on the number you want to receive. But experienced sellers know that a successful transaction involves much more than agreeing on a price. The amount of cash changing hands, the financing structure, the buyer’s ability to operate the business, and the expectations of both parties can all influence whether a deal actually comes together. The key is finding a structure that makes sense for both sides. A buyer may be willing to pay a strong price for a good business, but the amount of cash required upfront can have a significant impact on whether the transaction is workable. Seller financing can sometimes bridge that gap. Rather than requiring the buyer to provide the entire purchase price in cash at closing, a seller may finance a portion of the purchase. This can make the business accessible to a larger pool of qualified buyers while giving the seller the opportunity to receive payments over time. For buyers, the question is often simple: Can this business support the purchase price and provide enough income to make the investment worthwhile? For sellers, there’s a similar question: Can I structure the transaction in a way that gives the buyer a realistic chance to succeed while still achieving my financial goals? The best deal structure considers both. Qualified Buyers Matter Not every person who expresses interest in buying a business is ready or able to complete a transaction. A serious buyer should have a realistic understanding of the financial commitment involved, the responsibilities of ownership, and what it will take to operate the company successfully. This is one reason buyer qualification is such an important part of the selling process. A seller doesn’t simply need someone who likes the business. They need a buyer who has the financial resources, motivation, and ability to move forward. A qualified buyer also gives the seller greater confidence when considering terms such as seller financing. description: Seller Articles Does Your Asking Price Help or Hurt Your Business Sale? by Deal Studio on September 18, 2026 One of the most important decisions a business owner makes when preparing to sell is determining the right asking price. It is natural to want the highest possible value for a company built through years of hard work, sacrifice, and dedication. However, the market ultimately determines what a business is worth. Setting an asking price based on the company’s financial performance, strengths, and current market conditions is one of the best ways to attract qualified buyers. Some sellers take the approach of starting with a higher asking price and lowering it later if necessary. While this may seem like a reasonable strategy, it can create challenges. Buyers often use the asking price as their first indication of whether a business is a realistic opportunity. If the price does not align with the company’s earnings, assets, and market value, many qualified buyers may never take the time to explore further. An overpriced business can also spend more time on the market, causing buyers to question why it has not sold. A realistic asking price, on the other hand, can create more interest, encourage serious conversations, and lead to stronger negotiations. Determining the right price requires looking beyond what an owner hopes to receive. Buyers evaluate factors such as profitability, revenue trends, customer relationships, growth opportunities, operational systems, and risk. Two businesses in the same industry can have very different values depending on how they perform and how well they are positioned for future success. A business broker can provide valuable perspective throughout this process. While certain industries may experience periods of higher demand than others, buyers rarely make decisions based on industry alone. More often, they focus on the quality of the business itself. A well-managed company with strong financial performance will generally attract more interest than a struggling business in a “hot” industry. Understanding what buyers value can help owners make improvements long before they decide to sell. Buyers Look Beyond the Industry Every buyer has unique goals. Some are looking to expand an existing business, while others want to become business owners for the first time. Investment groups may be searching for companies with strong cash flow, while strategic buyers may value opportunities to grow through acquisition. Despite these different motivations, most buyers evaluate businesses using many of the same criteria. They want confidence that the business can continue to succeed after the ownership transition. Consistent profitability is often at the top of the list. Buyers also appreciate reliable cash flow, accurate financial records, and a business that has demonstrated stable performance over time. These factors help reduce uncertainty and make it easier for buyers and lenders to evaluate the opportunity. title: 12 Fatal Mistakes You Can Make When Selling Your Business
description: These are guidelines you will need to know when selling your business to achieve a faster transaction and the best possible price. 1) Lack of deal structure expertise When the seller has limited knowledge about the available alternatives for structuring the deal, he is at a definite disadvantage! And probably a costly one. Items such as leverage buy-outs, leases, royalties, earn-outs, consulting agreements, non-compete contracts can add immeasurable value and security to both buyer and seller alike. To understand more about the selling process and explore various deal structures, check out the SBA – Selling Your Business guide. 2) Failure to adjust the net owner benefit If you are to determine a proper value, the balance sheet and income statements must be recast. Items such as owner’s salary, depreciation, interest and fringe benefits may be added or subtracted depending on the circumstances. The adjusted income statement will reflect the actual owner benefit in order to help determine the market value. 3) Failure to maintain confidentiality Confidentiality is vital to the selling of a business. If employees know that you are selling and changes are coming, they may seek other opportunities. Competitors may use this information as a selling tool. Vendors may not continue to extend favorable terms. Profitability and market value may be reduced. 4) Failure to secure qualified buyers Knowing how to qualify a buyer is critical. We pre-qualifies each buyer to avoid a negotiation that is doomed to fail. This saves you time and money. It can eliminate hundreds of wasted hours and misdirected efforts. 5) Failure to continue to run your business It is important to maintain your business at peak operating capacity. The performance and productivity of your business is what you are really selling. title: Buyers Due Dilligence Checklist
description: Once a Buyer is committed to closing on the sale of a business, there is much to do. The list of tasks varies greatly depending the type, size and complexity of the business, the Buyer’s preferences and the legal requirements to own and operate the specific business being acquired. Although most Sellers are very helpful and obligated contractually to assist in the transfer of the business, practically speaking it is up to the Buyer to hire an accountant, seek legal advice from an attorney and take all of the appropriate steps to make sure they meet all of the legal requirements to own and operate the business at the time they assume ownership. Some of the items on a checklist that may need completed prior to buying an existing business may include: Consult an Attorney to set up the appropriate legal structure to own the business and reduce personal liability. The most common legal structures for owning a Florida business are a Subchapter-S Corporation or Limited Liability Company (LLC). Select a business trade name and determine if you need to register the business name with a fictitious name filing. Owners conducting business under a name other than their own may need to file, even if the name seems very similar. Speak with an Accountant regarding the tax implications of the legal structure and the allocation of the businesses purchase price. The accountant can apply for an Employer ID Number (EIN) Open a commercial bank account for your operating and/or payroll account(s) Decide if you will do in-house payroll or use a payroll service or employee leasing service. Many of these services offer complete human resources departments and all of the payroll tax and unemployment tax required filings quarterly and annually Set up a credit card vendor/machine Apply for Department of Revenue Sales Tax License Determine which licenses the business presently has and make sure they are current and valid at the time of sale. title: Stop being the last step ineveryprocess.
description: COMMON QUESTIONS Your questions, answered directly. If something is unclear after reading through these, the next step is a conversation. We want to understand where your practice is before recommending anything. START A CONVERSATION Do I have to take everything, or can I start with one piece? You start with either the website or the CRM. Deal management is its own software, tied to the CRM, so it arrives with the CRM rather than being a separate starting point. Whichever you begin with is built to connect to the rest, so adding the next piece later is an extension rather than a rebuild. Who designs and builds the website? The Deal Studio design team. It starts with a Brand Sprint to settle your positioning and messaging, then we handle the design, the build, the hosting, and the ongoing updates, and we wire it into your CRM as part of the build rather than afterward. What is a Brand Sprint? A focused working session before design starts. We work through who you serve, what you want to be known for, and how you talk about it, and the site gets built from what comes out of it. Its job is a website that says something specific about you from the day it launches rather than something generic. It is deliberately narrow: the Sprint settles the site, and it does not produce a brand guide. How is that different from a full brand engagement? Depth, and what comes out the other side. The Sprint settles positioning and messaging so the website can launch as something specific to you. A full brand engagement goes further: research into your market and the people you are trying to reach, positioning developed from the ground up, and a brand system built around connected outcomes, where one guide goes on to produce campaigns, content, resources, and new opportunities rather than a single website. Your type of license will depend on a couple of things: • What kind of establishment you have • The kind of alcohol you sell and what time of day  you sell it • Whether you’re planning to let customers roll BYOB-style or serving and selling alcohol • Where drinking occurs The two major types of licenses are an on-premise , where the liquor or alcoholic beverages you sell will be consumed on the premises, like a bar or restaurant. The other is an off-premise , which you need if you’re planning to have the liquor you sell be consumed off the premises, like a grocery store or drug store, or even a liquor store. There might be different qualifications for a catering company or special events. You’ll be applying for a specific class of license. title: Veterinary Practices For Sale
description:
About us Connecting veterinarians and practices since 1977.
Simmons & Associates prides itself in providing expertise for buying, selling and appraising veterinary practices. Simmons specializes exclusively in veterinary practice sales, appraisals, brokering and consultation. No individual or firm has helped more veterinarians achieve their dreams of buying their own practice or reaping the rewards of their efforts by offering their veterinary practice for sale.

With 11 national offices, we have local business advisors who are committed to setting new standards of excellence for the profession overall. title: HOW TO QUALIFY FOR A LAS VEGAS HOME LOAN
description: HOW TO QUALIFY FOR A LAS VEGAS HOME LOAN ☰ MORTGAGE LOANS MORTGAGE LOANS FINANCING FAQ BUYING FAQ MILITARY CONNECTION RELOCATION SERVICES OLD REPUBLIC HOME PROTECTION HUD HOMES HOW TO QUALIFY FOR A LAS VEGAS HOME LOAN Qualifying for Las Vegas mortgage loans is an important step in buying a home. Understanding the process can help ensure that you are able to qualify for the home loan that you need. Lenders look at two things when determining if you are able to qualify for a home loan: your ability to repay the loan and your willingness to repay it. Ability to repay The first thing that a lender wants to know is if you are able to repay the loan for which you are applying. The lender looks at your current employment. Have you been in the same job for at least two years or at least the same line of work for a few years? This shows the lender that you have steady employment, and its a great plus in qualifying for a home loan. The lender also looks at your total income and compares it to your debts, adding in your proposed monthly mortgage payment. You must have sufficient income to comfortably make these payments. This reflects your ability to repay the loan when qualifying for a home loan. If the lender believes your debt load is too high, you will qualify for a smaller loan and likely be charged a higher interest rate. Therefore, it makes sense to pay off as much debt as possible before applying for a home loan. Willingness to repay The next step in qualifying for a home loan is determining your willingness to repay the loan. Lenders determine this by looking at how you have paid off debt in the past, and it is one reason why lenders check your credit report. If you have faithfully made on-time payments toward your past debts, it helps you when qualifying for a home loan. The lender also looks at how you intend to use the property that you are buying. title: HOW TO QUALIFY FOR A LAS VEGAS HOME LOAN
description: HOW TO QUALIFY FOR A LAS VEGAS HOME LOAN ☰ MORTGAGE LOANS MORTGAGE LOANS FINANCING FAQ BUYING FAQ MILITARY CONNECTION RELOCATION SERVICES OLD REPUBLIC HOME PROTECTION HUD HOMES HOW TO QUALIFY FOR A LAS VEGAS HOME LOAN Qualifying for Las Vegas mortgage loans is an important step in buying a home. Understanding the process can help ensure that you are able to qualify for the home loan that you need. Lenders look at two things when determining if you are able to qualify for a home loan: your ability to repay the loan and your willingness to repay it. Ability to repay The first thing that a lender wants to know is if you are able to repay the loan for which you are applying. The lender looks at your current employment. Have you been in the same job for at least two years or at least the same line of work for a few years? This shows the lender that you have steady employment, and its a great plus in qualifying for a home loan. The lender also looks at your total income and compares it to your debts, adding in your proposed monthly mortgage payment. You must have sufficient income to comfortably make these payments. This reflects your ability to repay the loan when qualifying for a home loan. If the lender believes your debt load is too high, you will qualify for a smaller loan and likely be charged a higher interest rate. Therefore, it makes sense to pay off as much debt as possible before applying for a home loan. Willingness to repay The next step in qualifying for a home loan is determining your willingness to repay the loan. Lenders determine this by looking at how you have paid off debt in the past, and it is one reason why lenders check your credit report. If you have faithfully made on-time payments toward your past debts, it helps you when qualifying for a home loan. The lender also looks at how you intend to use the property that you are buying. title: Key Biscayne MLS Listing A12005335
description: About this Property 485 W Matheson Drive is one of America’s most iconic waterfront estates, representing a rare convergence of presidential history, cinematic legacy, and unparalleled waterfront scale. Set on approximately 2.38 acres with an extraordinary 862’ of direct Biscayne Bay frontage, the property captures sweeping, unobstructed views of the Miami skyline and open bay, offering a level of presence and exclusivity rarely found in South Florida. Once the “Winter White House” of, the estate also achieved cinematic fame as the Frank Lopez residence in Scarface, with original architectural elements still preserved, including the iconic glass elevator. Offers 5BR + gym (can be converted to 6th BR) 7+2BA, and approximately 13,500 SF (per owner) across three levels, featuring soaring 24’+ ceilings, marble floors, and walls of glass framing breathtaking bay views. Expansive living, dining, and kitchen areas open to large terraces, creating seamless indoor-outdoor living ideal for both everyday comfort and grand-scale entertaining. Resort-style grounds include a piano-shaped saltwater pool, cabana bath, lush tropical landscaping, and expansive lawn areas with artfully integrated lighting extending the estate’s experience well beyond sunset. A private marina, formerly a presidential helipad—features rare 3-phase power and dockage for yachts up to 200’, plus over 34,000 SF of submerged land, making this one of Miami’s most significant and irreplaceable waterfront holdings in the world.
