Seamless indoor and outdoor living creates an inviting atmosphere for any size gathering. Fantastic Sunrise pool and spa overlooking ocean. The courtyard features stunning 65' Sunset pool, spacious terrace, and loggia. Expansive manicured grounds with lush tropical landscaping allowing for the utmost privacy. Sprawling dunes showcasing the expansive views of the Atlantic Ocean. Ideal for car collectors, the home also features 6+ car garages. Creating a one-of-a-kind approach, the estate is entered via a gently winding driveway, arriving at a spectacular property meant for the true connoisseur of Palm Beach Living.

title: Palm Beach MLS Listing B26069003
description: About this Property Spectacular Ocean-to-Lake estate in Palm Beach's coveted Estate Section with nearly 30,000 total square feet. Built new in 2024, this sprawling residence is nestled on nearly 2 acres and boasts breathtaking views of the Atlantic Ocean and Intracoastal Waterway. A gracious floorplan offers 7 bedrooms, 12 full bathrooms, and a powder room. An impressive great room features soaring volume ceilings, fireplace, and abundant natural light. The beautifully appointed kitchen features an oversized island, spacious butler's pantry, top-of-the-line appliances, and breakfast room. Additional interior highlights include a playroom, club room, and office, providing exceptional flexibility for both everyday living and entertaining. The expansive Primary Wing features a private sitting area with lakefront balcony, dual bathrooms and dressing rooms, morning bar, and oceanfront terrace. Additional en-suite bedrooms offer generous accommodations for guests. The second floor also includes two laundry rooms, a lounge/additional guest suite, and multiple balconies overlooking the water and grounds.  The lower level is designed for both function and recreation, with ample storage, a large exercise room, spa bath and sauna, memorabilia room, and expansive 18+/- car garage ideal for the avid collector. Beautifully landscaped and impeccably maintained grounds stretch from the Ocean to the Intracoastal. Multiple terraces and covered loggias surround the 53-foot infinity swimming pool with sun shelf, creating exceptional spaces for outdoor entertaining and relaxation. Convenient service drive, as well as an oversized driveway leading to additional 3 car garage. A private dock with boat lift completes this extraordinary waterfront offering.  A truly remarkable Ocean-to-Lake residence offering grand-scale living, sophisticated design, resort-style amenities, and an unparalleled Palm Beach waterfront lifestyle.

description: Every potential transaction (or often there can be a dispute) requires a different type of business valuation. Three Types of Business Valuations Every potential transaction (or often, a dispute) requires a different type of business valuation . Some business valuations can be complex, so getting the correct valuation for the proper purpose is critical. In broad terms, there are three types of business valuations: 1. Broker’s Opinion of Value (BOV) If a business owner is considering a sale, you’ll likely want a Broker’s Opinion of Value (BOV). This report combines a Most Probable Selling Price (MPSP) for the business using three valuation methods – Market Data, Income , and Cost or Asset Approach. A Broker’s Opinion of Value will provide a starting point for setting a price if you are considering selling or buying a business. To see a sample Broker’s Opinion of Value, click here. 2. Standard Informational Valuation The Standard Informational Valuation is a non-certified report that provides a business’s value based on financial performance, market variables, comparable sales data, and industry expertise. It indicates what a Buyer would be willing to pay for the company in the open market. Within this report, you will find a market-based valuation based on sales, SDE (Seller’s Discretionary Earnings), EBITDA multiples , and the asset value of your company. The valuation explains the use of different methods and each calculation. The report includes the company’s historical financial details, as well as adjustments to these financials, which form the basis of the valuation. You will see a “likely” or “suggested” price based on the median value of the comparable transactions. The business’s value will likely fall within a range or be close to the company’s final sale price. This report, typically over 35 pages long, is best suited for individuals who do not require a certified valuation and are comfortable with more limited procedures and reporting. This type of valuat

title: Business Valuation
description: Every potential transaction (or often there can be a dispute) requires a different type of business valuation. Three Types of Business Valuations Every potential transaction (or often, a dispute) requires a different type of business valuation . Some business valuations can be complex, so getting the correct valuation for the proper purpose is critical. In broad terms, there are three types of business valuations: 1. Broker’s Opinion of Value (BOV) If a business owner is considering a sale, you’ll likely want a Broker’s Opinion of Value (BOV). This report combines a Most Probable Selling Price (MPSP) for the business using three valuation methods – Market Data, Income , and Cost or Asset Approach. A Broker’s Opinion of Value will provide a starting point for setting a price if you are considering selling or buying a business. To see a sample Broker’s Opinion of Value, click here. 2. Standard Informational Valuation The Standard Informational Valuation is a non-certified report that provides a business’s value based on financial performance, market variables, comparable sales data, and industry expertise. It indicates what a Buyer would be willing to pay for the company in the open market. Within this report, you will find a market-based valuation based on sales, SDE (Seller’s Discretionary Earnings), EBITDA multiples , and the asset value of your company. The valuation explains the use of different methods and each calculation. The report includes the company’s historical financial details, as well as adjustments to these financials, which form the basis of the valuation. You will see a “likely” or “suggested” price based on the median value of the comparable transactions. The business’s value will likely fall within a range or be close to the company’s final sale price. This report, typically over 35 pages long, is best suited for individuals who do not require a certified valuation and are comfortable with more limited procedures and reporting. This type of valuat

title: Answers to the most common questions from buyers and sellers
description: Frequently Asked Questions Everything you need to know How much is my business worth? A business valuation depends on factors like cash flow, industry, growth trends, customer concentration, financial cleanliness, and market demand. We provide a free, confidential valuation to help you understand your true market value. Can I sell my business if I have debt or loans? Yes. In most cases, outstanding loans or debt are paid off at closing from the sale proceeds. If the debt is less than the value of the business, this is typically not an issue. Obtaining an opinion of value before going to market is key to understanding your options. Will my employees or competitors find out the business is for sale? No. We maintain strict confidentiality throughout the entire process. Buyers sign NDAs before receiving any identifying information. Can I offer seller financing when selling my business? Yes. Seller financing is common and can make your business more attractive to buyers by reducing their upfront capital requirements. It often leads to faster closings and can sometimes result in a higher sale price. Your advisor can help you structure terms that protect your interests Will a buyer need to qualify for SBA financing? Many buyers use SBA loans to purchase businesses under $5 million. Understanding how buyers get financing helps you evaluate offers and avoid deals that fall through. Our team works closely with lenders to ensure buyers are pre-qualified before moving forward. What types of businesses do you work with? We specialize in small to mid-market companies across manufacturing, service, construction, technology, healthcare, food & beverage, agriculture, and more. Do I need a business broker to sell my business? While you can sell independently, working with an experienced advisor typically results in a higher sale price, faster process, and better qualified buyers—and reduces risk during negotiations and due diligence while managing confidentiality. The ROI of Outdoor Maintenance: What Homeowners Should Know
description: The ROI of Outdoor Maintenance: What Homeowners Should Know Dated: May 6 2026 Views: 1339 When it comes to maximizing your home’s value, outdoor and exterior maintenance, including lawn and landscaping, are an overlooked opportunity. Regular lawn care services, landscape maintenance, exterior maintenance, and tree trimming increase curb appeal and have above-average ROI. Here’s how much each task returns on your investment to help you decide which ones fit your schedule and budget. 1. Keep up With Routine Lawn Care Services: 217% ROI First impressions are important, and homebuyers’ first judgment of your home starts with the first thing they see: the lawn. The National Association of Realtors ( NAR ) finds that regular lawn maintenance can yield up to a 217% ROI for homeowners. To achieve this ROI, schedule recurring fertilizer and/or weed control applications throughout the year. This ensures that your lawn grows strong and resists weeds in every season, so your lawn looks healthy and uniform, even if you’re selling in the off-season . 2. Maintain Your Landscaping: 104% ROI Homebuyers don’t just look at the lawn – they also look at the landscaping. NAR expects an ROI of about 104% for the following tasks: annual mulching, mowing the lawn, shrub pruning, and planting about 60 perennials or annuals. According to a 2019 study , curb appeal can boost your home’s value by as much as 7%, or up to 14% in cold (slow) markets. On the low end, that adds about $21,000 to a home selling for $299,000. 3. Maintain Your Home Exterior: Up to 268% ROI Neglected exteriors may indicate expensive maintenance or renovation costs and can be a dealbreaker for homebuyers. Conversely, a tidy, well-maintained exterior creates an appealing prospect for homebuyers.
